originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq jumps over 1% as chip stocks rally, investors eye AI earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: The US stock market had a good day, with the Nasdaq index going up by over 1%. This was partly because companies that make computer chips, like Broadcom, did well due to excitement about artificial intelligence. However, Microsoft's stock went down after the company announced it would be cutting jobs. Investors are now waiting to see how companies do in their upcoming earnings reports and what the Federal Reserve (the "Fed") will do with interest rates. This will help them decide what to do with their investments.

originalTitle: NY Fed says supply chain pressures eased in June
simplifiedContent: The New York Fed, which is part of the US central bank, tracks how well things are moving through global supply chains. Recently, they found that things got a bit better in June, with their index score going down to 1.25. This is good news because it means that problems in the Middle East, like blocked shipping routes, are starting to clear up. As a result, oil prices might stay lower, which could help keep inflation (or price rises) under control. This matters because lower inflation can be good for the economy and for people who buy and sell stocks.

originalTitle: EasyJet shares reveal deal risk as $7.3 billion takeover advances
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening with EasyJet: the company has agreed to be taken over by another company called Castlelake in a £5.5 billion deal. EasyJet's stock price went up after the news, but it's still lower than what Castlelake is offering to pay. This is because some people are worried that the deal might not happen due to rules about who can own companies in the EU, or because shareholders might not agree to it. The deal isn't final yet, and Castlelake has until August 3 to make a formal offer. This means there's still some uncertainty and risk that the takeover might not go through.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold tops $4,200, silver nears $64 as recovery rally extends; Fed minutes in focus
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver went up a bit on July 6th. This happened because people are less worried that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, and the value of the US dollar has gone down. As a result, gold futures (a type of investment in gold) reached $4,215 and silver reached $63.73, which is an improvement from their previous prices. This is important because it shows that investors are still interested in buying gold and silver, even after they had lost some value. The prices may continue to change as investors wait to see what the Federal Reserve will do next.

originalTitle: Trent Q1 business update: Revenue grows 19%, store network expands
simplifiedContent: Trent, a company owned by the Tata Group, recently shared an update on its business performance. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it made, increased by 19% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹5,666 crore. This is a good sign for the company, and it also expanded its number of stores to 1,312. As a result, the company's stock price, which had previously gone down, bounced back up by 17.2% this year. This increase in revenue and expansion of stores suggests that the company is doing well, which is why its stock price is rising.

originalTitle: Rentomojo gets SEBI nod for raising funds through IPO launch. Details here
simplifiedContent: Rentomojo, a company that rents out furniture, has gotten approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch an Initial Public Offering (IPO). This means the company can now raise money from the public by selling shares. The IPO will allow existing shareholders to sell their shares, and the company plans to use the money it raises (up to ₹150 crore) to expand and pay off debts. This is important because it shows that Rentomojo is growing and has a significant presence in India's online rental market. The IPO will give the company the funds it needs to continue expanding its business.
